criteria.question: What first-party source defines LangGraph checkpoint, checkpointer, thread, namespace, metadata, version, or state persistence contracts relevant to durable resume?
What first-party source demonstrates interrupt, resume, replay, pending writes, or durable execution behavior, and what identity must remain stable across resume?
What first-party source describes checkpointer storage implementations, serialization, persistence guarantees, or conformance tests that can be isolated behind an adapter?
What first-party source establishes the JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js integration surface, package boundaries, runtime requirements, or supported persistence adapters?
What first-party source establishes what LangGraph owns versus what a host product must retain for execution authority, approvals, credentials, sandboxing, evidence, or lifecycle?
What first-party source reveals extension, replacement, version, or migration boundaries needed to remove a LangGraph checkpoint adapter without changing the native host semantics?
